_about: Chapter R (Resolve) of the suite results document: the prose data of DESIGN-DOC.md section 5 for manifest v4 (units as in units_v4.json). `intro` is the chapter page, in paragraphs; `families` keys on the family id (the scenario id prefix) with a title and one paragraph of prose (what the family checks, why, the ground truth, known caveats); `units` keys on the unit id with its one-line property. Keys are family and unit ids, never scenario ids, so a new scenario of an existing unit is covered. Plain text, no markup: the generator escapes for LaTeX. Every claim follows SPEC-labeled-traversal-core.md section 4, areas.py gen_R and checks.py as of c11db9dd; recorded facts are the v4 run's (20261014T061053Z, re-evaluated with c11db9dd). The check catalogue is in checks.json (shared by every chapter), the glossary in glossary.json.
title: Resolve
intro: POST /resolve maps a query to the labels that carry it (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 4). For a query of L bases the host maps its L - k + 1 k-mers to the graph (on this basic graph the forward strand only) and reports `graph_runs`, the maximal runs of consecutive k-mers that are in the graph, as 0-based half-open intervals of k-mer starts; `num_kmers` is L - k + 1. For each requested label it reports the k-mers the label supports, as runs of the same form and as a count, `kmers_supported`. A column label (a taxid) supports a k-mer when the k-mer is in the graph and the label is in its annotation row; a header label (an accession.version) when some coordinate of its column at that row maps to that sequence; with support trace a header label additionally requires consecutive supported k-mers to have consecutive coordinates, so a coordinate jump ends the run (section 4.2). Each pair of a k-mer and a label is thus in one of three states, absent from the graph, in the graph without the label, in the graph with it, and a label not asked for is never reported.

A request names exactly one of labels (explicit, one or more column or header names) or discover. A discovery collects the labels of every in-graph k-mer's row (kind column or header), ranks them by supported k-mers and keeps the top `max_labels` (ties by column id, then sequence id), stating `labels_truncated` (kept, total, the least support kept, the most support dropped, and how many dropped labels supported every k-mer) when more labels occurred than it kept. The candidates and the optional select block, the seed selection for /traverse (section 4.3), are not exercised by this chapter.

The time budget (section 4.5) is opt-in: `bounds.time_budget_ms`, a number above the finalisation reserve of 250 ms, lowered to the server's cap (60,000 ms on staging) and stated in limits.clamped when lowered. The work reads the deadline between its row batches and its pieces of k-mers and stops at the budget less the reserve; a stop answers, with status 200, exactly the resolve of a prefix of the query, its first `resolved_kmers` k-mers, with a stop block (phase, reason time, `resolved_kmers`, `query_kmers`, `resolved_bp`, `remainder_from_bp`) beside limits, so that a client resolves the rest from `remainder_from_bp`. The answer is built within the reserve; past the budget it is a 503 with the code deadline, never a partial answer. The pieces the deadline cannot interrupt (the request's parse, the mapping of the query's k-mers, one row batch's decode, the explicit labels' resolution) can push a stop or a 503 past the budget; the suite reads that as a finding only beyond max(1 s, the budget) (appendix A, `budget_respected`). Validation is strict: an unknown field, a wrong type, a value out of range, both or neither of labels and discover, a duplicate or an unknown label, a query shorter than k or longer than the server's or the request's `max_query_bp` are 400s naming the problem.

Ground truth. The windows are cut from the records of I.1; the record's taxid column and its accession.version are the labels, and every k-mer of a window cut from the record is in the graph and supported by both. Lengths run from k (one k-mer) to 2,000 bp, the cap the service sends on every explicit-label resolve; the 10 kb stops of R-budget run up to the server's limit of 10,000 bp and reach the host on the direct arms only. Every explicit-label request of the chapter names `bounds.time_budget_ms` 20,000 and `bounds.max_query_bp` 2,000 (a discovery names `max_query_bp` 500 and no budget), as the service sends them, so that the direct arms and the MCP arm ask the same question. Two caveats hold for the whole chapter: on this basic graph a k-mer and its reverse complement are different nodes, so a reverse-complemented window is another query (R-rc); and under a budget the host's answer depends on the machine's load, a 503 deadline being allowed wherever the request names a budget and reading inconclusive, never pass.

Via MCP a resolve is the `traverse_resolve` tool, a job the service runs in its queue (the table's case `resolve.job_path`): the tool waits for the answer inline, up to 30 s with explicit labels and 10 s for a discovery, and otherwise hands back a job the runner polls to its end. The service validates first and in its own terms: it always sends its own `bounds.max_query_bp` (2,000; 500 for a discovery) and refuses a longer query at submit, so the 10 kb scenarios cannot be expressed; it de-duplicates labels, upper-cases the sequence, and refuses any character outside ACGT, more than 1,000 distinct labels, a budget below 500 ms or above the host's cap, and a discovery limit outside 1..100; support, select and graph have no argument. Chapter R's MCP column therefore holds many by-design and not-implemented glyphs. Appendix B names every case with the service's code and text, and a by-design pair is verified against the direct arms' answers; the 2,000 bp window of pfa, which the service's 30 s inline wait ended once under load (`resolve_timeout`, a host state), is the chapter's one inconclusive MCP execution.

R-pos.title: positive windows
R-pos.prose: Windows of 31, 32, 50, 100, 200, 1,000 and 2,000 bp cut from the records, two records per length, resolved under the record's own taxid column and under its header label. The property is the simplest claim /resolve makes and the ground every other chapter stands on: every k-mer of a window taken from a record is in the graph and supported by that record's labels, as one run covering the whole query (`resolve_runs`, full), and `graph_runs` is that same single run (`resolve_graph_runs`). The lengths bracket the k-mer count from one (31 bp) and two (32 bp) to 1,970 (2,000 bp, the cap the service sends). Each request names the 20,000 ms budget, so a 503 deadline is allowed under load and reads inconclusive; the one such case of this run, the 2,000 bp window of pfa on direct-local (a 503 at 24 s) and on the cold MCP call (the service's `resolve_timeout`), sits in the detail block of its unit, the warm executions of both arms having passed. The four units are the column and header halves over the two record sets (A: eco, mtb, pae, cje, mge, ser, hvo; B: buc, mpn, mja, sso, spo, scem, pfa).

R-multi.title: several labels
R-multi.prose: One 100 bp window per scenario resolved under three labels at once: the record's taxid column, its header, and the taxid column of a record from another kingdom. The record's two labels must support every k-mer (`resolve_runs`, full, once per label); the unrelated column must not support all of them (`label_not_full`). The second claim rests on the assumption that a random, DUST-filtered 100 bp window of one kingdom has at least one k-mer that a genome of another kingdom lacks; a window from a gene conserved across kingdoms would break it, and the truth of each scenario states so. Together with R-order this is the evidence that labels in one request are answered independently of each other.

R-junction.title: junctions
R-junction.prose: The concatenation of two 100 bp windows from records of different kingdoms, resolved under both taxid columns. The expected runs are computed from the records, not assumed: A's column has the run [0, `a_end`), where `a_end` is 70 plus the number of B's leading bases that happen to repeat A's own continuation in its record (at most k - 1), and B's column has [`b_start`, 170), where `b_start` is 100 less the number of A's trailing bases that repeat what precedes B's window in its record. `resolve_runs` asks for exactly these runs, so a label whose run reaches into the other record's k-mers is a wrong answer. A junction k-mer that another record of the same column happens to hold would move a run end; the builder does not model that, and the four junctions of this run end at 70, 70, 71 and 76 for A and start at 98, 99, 100 and 100 for B.

R-discover.title: discovery
R-discover.prose: A 100 bp window from a record with few relatives in RefSeq (a low-carrier genome: buc, mge, mpn, ser, mja, sso) resolved without labels, discovering column labels or header labels with `max_labels` 1, 20 or 100 (`bounds.max_query_bp` 500 and no time budget, as the service sends a discovery; a discovery reads every in-graph k-mer's whole row). The property (`resolve_discover_contains`) is that the source record's own label, its taxid column or its accession.version, is listed. The source supports every in-graph k-mer of the query, so a truncated list may leave it out only in a tie at that full support, which the check verifies from `labels_truncated` (the least support kept and the most support dropped both equal to the in-graph k-mer count, at least one dropped label at full length), the ranking being all the answer can show: the tie is decided by column id, then sequence id, which the answer does not state. The invariants also require the list ranked by support, at most `max_labels` long and `labels_truncated` consistent with it. With `max_labels` 1 the source is regularly outranked in a tie (R-discover-0001 of this run: kept 1 of 9 labels at 70 k-mers each); that passes, as SPEC section 4.2's tie rule says.

R-trace.title: trace support
R-trace.prose: 200 bp of a record resolved under its header with support trace: beyond presence, consecutive supported k-mers must have consecutive coordinates in that sequence (SPEC section 4.2), so a window cut from the record is exactly one contiguous run over every k-mer (`resolve_runs`, full). The three records, E. coli, S. aureus and phage lambda, differ in the size of their column and in the number of records it holds. The `traverse_resolve` tool has no support argument, so this family is not implemented via MCP.

R-budget.title: the time budget
R-budget.prose: 10 kb of a record (E. coli under 3,000 ms, P. aeruginosa under 8,000 ms; windows drawn without the uniqueness requirement and with the DUST threshold raised to 5) under a budget chosen so that the work stops inside the query on a cold or loaded host and completes on a warm one. The property is the stated stop of SPEC section 4.5: the answer is the resolve of a prefix, its stop block consistent (`num_kmers` equal to `resolved_kmers`, `resolved_bp` and `remainder_from_bp` derived from it, the stop at or after the budget less the reserve), and the record's own label supports every k-mer of that prefix as one run (`resolve_runs`, full with `prefix_if_stopped`). A complete answer never exercised the property and reads inconclusive; a 503 deadline is allowed and reads inconclusive, or a finding when it comes more than max(1 s, the budget) late (`budget_respected`). The two twins of each stop, the same 10 kb under 20,000 ms (R-twin-0002 and -0004, full unless stopped) and its second half from base 5,000 (R-twin-0003 and -0005), are what the `prefix_equals` relations compare the stop against: on their common k-mers the graph runs and the label's runs must be the same sets. Known caveats: on this host under the Logan load the two stops and the full 20 s twin of eco answered 503 on both direct arms, between 1 and 25 s past their budgets (findings where more than max(1 s, the budget) late: the query's k-mer mapping and one row batch are not polled), and the full twin of pae answered 503 on direct-local and completed host-warm on direct-remote in 0.4 s. The stated stop has not been observed on this host, so the prefix property and three of the four relations read inconclusive, and the v4 deploy gate declares `REL-prefix_equals-0001` to -0003 excluded on direct-local for that reason. The MCP cannot express a 10 kb resolve (the service's cap is 2,000 bp): every MCP call was refused at submit by design, and the column reads not implemented, as the table's case `resolve.not_expressible.bounds_max_query_bp` says.

R-edge.title: edge inputs
R-edge.prose: The edges of /resolve's validation and of its alphabet, one input each, on 100 bp of E. coli unless the edge is the length. Refused inputs expect the host's exact 400 text, or its prefix where the text carries a value: k - 1 bases, 10,001 bp (above the server's limit of 10,000), 200 bp above a request bound of 100, an unknown label (named), a duplicate label (refused, not merged, as the source decides), an empty sequence, discover together with labels and neither of the two, an unknown field (named), graph and graphs on a single-graph server, a body that is not an object and one that is not JSON, a budget not above the 250 ms reserve, and `discover.max_labels` 0. Accepted inputs expect a 200 with the right profile: exactly k bases (one k-mer, `graph_runs` [[0, 1]]); an N or an IUPAC R at position 50, which /resolve does not refuse, the 31 k-mers holding it being absent from the graph (`graph_runs` [[0, 20], [51, 70]]) and the label supporting the 39 others; lower case, resolved as upper case; 1,001 explicit labels, which the host does not cap; a random 200 bp with no k-mer in the graph (`resolve_absent`); a budget of 70,000 ms lowered to the server's 60,000 and stated (clamped); and the two split cases the service refuses but the host answers, `discover.max_labels` 150 and a budget of 400 ms. The texts of the refusals were read from the source where no smoke run had exercised them (tag code-derived). Via MCP most of the family is decided by the service: seven inputs cannot be expressed (a request bound other than the service's, the 10,001 bp query the service refuses at its own 2,000 before the host's limit applies, an unknown field, graph, graphs, the two protocol bodies); the service refuses eleven at submit and relays the host's refusal of two more (k - 1 bases, the unknown label) under its own code; it de-duplicates the labels of R-edge-0009 and answers where the host refuses; it upper-cases R-edge-0007 and the answers agree. Each such pair is a by-design case that appendix B names and the comparison verifies.

R-rc.title: reverse complement
R-rc.prose: The reverse complement of a 100 bp window that occurs once on either strand of its record (S. aureus, M. jannaschii), resolved under the record's header. On this basic graph a k-mer and its reverse complement are different nodes and the index holds the records' forward strands, so the header supports none of the query's k-mers: `kmers_supported` 0, the label still listed (`resolve_runs` with kmers 0). The k-mers may or may not be in the graph through other genomes; the check does not ask. This is the resolve-side statement of the strand fact that chapters P, T and N test on their routes.

R-order.title: label order
R-order.prose: The labels of an R-multi request in another order (header, unrelated column, taxid) on a 100 bp window of H. volcanii: the taxid column and the header support every k-mer as when they are named first. `resolve_runs` reads a label by its name, so the check is order-blind by construction; the scenario tests that the host is too.

R-twin.title: twins
R-twin.prose: The upper-case twin of the lower-case resolve R-edge-0007: the same 100 bp of E. coli in upper case, expected full under the column, and the relation `same_answer`, which requires the two bodies to be equal apart from timing, on every arm (via MCP the service upper-cases the lower-case request before the host sees it, so the two answers are the same there too). The other twins made for relations, the full and the continued 10 kb resolves, are printed with R-budget, whose relations they serve.

units.R-pos-column-A: A window cut from the record resolves fully under the record's taxid column: every k-mer supported, one run [0, L - k + 1), `graph_runs` the same run.
units.R-pos-column-B: The same property on the second record of each length (buc, mpn, mja, sso, spo, scem, pfa).
units.R-pos-header-A: A window cut from the record resolves fully under the record's header label (accession.version): every k-mer supported, one run [0, L - k + 1), `graph_runs` the same run.
units.R-pos-header-B: The same property on the second record of each length.
units.R-multi: Three labels in one request: the record's taxid column and its header support every k-mer (one run each); the other kingdom's column does not support all of them.
units.R-junction: Two 100 bp windows of different kingdoms concatenated: A's column has exactly the run [0, `a_end`) and B's exactly [`b_start`, 170), both ends computed from the records' own continuations.
units.R-discover: A discovery without labels lists the source record's label (column or header) within `max_labels`, or states a truncation that can hide it only in a tie at full support.
units.R-trace: support trace on 200 bp of the record under its own header: one contiguous run over every k-mer, the coordinates consecutive throughout.
units.R-budget: A 10 kb resolve under a small budget stops with a stated prefix the record's label fully supports, or answers 503 deadline (allowed: inconclusive); its twins, the full 20 s resolve and the continuation from base 5,000, agree with it on their common k-mers (relations `prefix_equals`).
units.R-edge-refused: A malformed or out-of-bound request is refused with 400 and the exact text (or prefix) the host's source states, before any work.
units.R-edge-accepted: An edge input the host accepts is answered with the right profile: exactly k bases; an N or IUPAC code (its 31 k-mers absent, the rest supported); lower case; 1,001 labels; an absent random sequence; a budget above the cap lowered and stated; and the two values the service refuses but the host answers.
units.R-rc: The reverse complement of a window unique on both strands: on this basic, forward-strand graph the record's header supports none of its k-mers (`kmers_supported` 0).
units.R-order: The same labels in another order are each answered as if named alone.
units.R-twin-case: The lower-case resolve (R-edge-0007) and its upper-case twin answer byte for byte alike, timing aside (relation `same_answer`).
